papers.title_en: BioStudyBench: Evaluating Agents on Post-Cutoff Biomedical Studies
papers.authors: David Li, Shaamil Karim, Christian Gensbigler
papers.evidence: 评估智能体长周期生物医学研究能力的基准
papers.tldr: 现有评估难以区分AI智能体是真正分析数据，还是依赖先验知识或直接检索已发表答案。为此，作者提出BioStudyBench，从404,019条PubMed记录中半自动筛选出25个发表于2026年7-9月、晚于模型知识截止的生物医学长程分析任务。智能体仅获中性研究问题，须自行查找并下载公开数据、用仅返回截止前文献的工具检索，并通过数据分析报告发现。八个模型中，数据与工具使平均通过率较无数据基线提升47个百分点；最佳开源模型通过81.3%，最佳闭源模型94.7%。
papers.abstract_en: We evaluate whether AI agents can match the reported findings of published biomedical studies using public data. Existing evaluations do not consistently separate analysis from prior knowledge or retrieval of the published answer. We introduce BioStudyBench, a benchmark of 25 long-horizon analysis tasks drawn from studies first published between July and September 2026, after the developer-reported knowledge cutoffs of the models we evaluate, semi-automatically filtered down from 404,019 PubMed records. In each task, the agent receives a neutral research question but no data files, so it must find and download the relevant public data, search the literature through tools that return only records dated before its cutoff, and report findings through data analysis. To measure gains over prior knowledge, we run every task both with and without access to data and tools. Across eight models, access to data and tools raises the pass rate by 47 percentage points on average over the no-data baseline. Open-weight models across sizes trail closed-weight models, with the best open-weight model passing 81.3% of tasks against 94.7% for the best closed-weight model.

papers.title_en: MathAgent: Multi-Agent Optimization of Mathematical Invariants for Molecular Property Prediction
papers.authors: Yiming Ren, Josh V. Vermaas, Guo-Wei Wei
papers.evidence: 面向分子性质预测、优化不变量表示的LLM多智能体框架
papers.tldr: 分子性质预测中，数学不变量可提供互补表示，但最优组合随数据集与任务变化，手工筛选代价高。为此提出MathAgent，以语言模型推理协调任务解读、策略提议与流程，结合确定性工具完成计算与数值决策，并采用数据集感知设计、低成本候选筛选和渐进评估。在蛋白-配体结合亲和力与定量毒性预测上，不同数据集偏好不同不变量组合，证明需按数据集自适应选择。该框架提供了系统、可追溯且目标条件化的不变量优化途径。
papers.abstract_en: Mathematical invariants provide complementary representations of molecular structure, but their predictive utility can vary across datasets and prediction tasks. For a new dataset, appropriate construction of invariant representations from algebraic topology, differential geometry, topological spectral theory, and commutative algebra is a challenging task, particularly when evaluating multiple representations is computationally expensive. We develop a Mathematical Agentic Model (MathAgent) to automatically optimize invariant representations in molecular property prediction. The framework combines dataset-aware representation design, low-cost candidate screening, and progressive evaluation. Language-model reasoning supports task interpretation, strategy proposal, and workflow coordination, while scientific computations and numerical decisions are carried out by deterministic tools. We evaluate MathAgent on protein--ligand binding-affinity and quantitative toxicity prediction tasks. Different datasets favor different combinations of mathematical invariants, demonstrating the need for dataset-adaptive representation selection rather than a fixed universal representation. Objective-conditioned executions further show that the framework can adjust its evaluation strategy according to user-specified goals. MathAgent therefore provides a systematic, evidence-driven, and traceable approach for optimizing mathematical invariant representations and reducing reliance on manual configuration and/or experimentation in molecular property prediction.

papers.title_en: MedPrune: Topology-Efficient Multimodal Multi-Agent Communication Evolution for Medical VQA Tasks
papers.authors: Jiuheng Wan, Runze Li, Chen Chen, Tingyuan Hu, Daiyang Yu, Yimin Jing, Taolin Zhang, Richang Hong
papers.evidence: 面向医学视觉问答的高效多模态多智能体协作框架
papers.tldr: 面向医学VQA，现有多智能体框架常因冗余通信拓扑带来交互模式僵化与算力开销，限制推理与token效率。MedPrune将诊断过程建模为异质通信图，以专科智能体为节点、科室内外交互为边，并通过强化学习驱动的异质节点稀疏化与兼顾任务性能/拓扑复杂度的异质边稀疏化，动态裁剪节点和边。在全量及少样本医学VQA实验中，该方法超越多智能体基线，提升token效率并展现强对抗鲁棒性，为高效医学多模态协作提供新范式。
papers.abstract_en: While medical multimodal large language models (Med-MLLMs) advance medical visual question answering (VQA), existing clinical workflow-inspired multi-agent frameworks suffer from interaction patterns and excessive computational overhead caused by redundant communication topologies. In this paper, we propose MedPrune, an efficient medical multimodal multi-agent collaboration framework that dynamically prunes both nodes and edges from the communication topology to enhance reasoning ability and token efficiency. Specifically, we first formulate the diagnostic process as a heterogeneous communication graph, where nodes represent specialist agents from various departments and edges capture intra- and inter-departmental interactions. Building on this graph, we introduce two sparsification mechanisms to enable adaptive collaborative evolution: (1) Heterogeneous Node Sparsification, which eliminates task-irrelevant specialist agents irrelevant to the current multimodal question via reinforcement learning-driven topological optimization, and (2) Heterogeneous Edge Sparsification, which selectively retains only the most diagnostically salient intra- and inter-departmental connections by jointly optimizing task performance and topological complexity. Extensive medical VQA experiments under full-set and few-shot training settings prove MedPrune surpasses multi-agent baselines and boosts token efficiency with strong adversarial robustness.
